content.comment_body: Hello, how can I read registers via Modbus TCP from a device operating as a server? The device only supports Read Holding Registers (0x03) and Write Multiple Registers (0x10) function codes. I tried several methods based on different documents, but haven't succeeded. When I use QModMaster as a tester instead of [product_name], everything works: I can read and write registers without issues. I am quite new to [product_name].

You do not need to manually specify a function code for [product_name] in Modbus communication. The system automatically selects the correct function code, depending on whether you are reading or writing and how many words are involved.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are uncertain about configuring Modbus TCP communication on [product_name], especially regarding function codes for reading and writing registers. One user tried manually setting function codes for compatibility with another Modbus server, but [product_name] actually manages function codes automatically based on communication type. Documentation does not clearly explain this behavior, causing confusion and unsuccessful configuration attempts.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to be able to manually select function codes for Modbus register communication in [product_name], similar to their experience with third-party tools. They also anticipate clear instructions or interface options to configure these codes.
